transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Daniel Cho (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Head of AI, Veridian), Marcus Hale (Platform Eng, Veridian), Dr. Rakesh Mehta (Research Lead, Veridian)

Summary (auto):
Veridian is evaluating Redwood for clinical note summarization, adverse event detection, and an internal question-answering assistant. Main concerns: PHI/hipaa, context length for long patient histories (~80k tokens), multilingual Spanish/Portuguese support, tool-calling to a structured adverse-event DB and internal search. Leaning toward Dedicated or Private due to compliance but wants to validate hosted first for proof-of-concept. Next steps include security docs, pilot scope, and benchmark scripts.

Topics: model selection (open models), context window, multilingual, tool-calling, deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), compliance (HIPAA, KMS, audit logs)

Action items (mentioned in call): see metadata action_items above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Daniel: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, quick roll call, i'm daniel from redwood, priya's here too, how's it going lena?
[00:06] Lena: hi daniel hi priya, good thanks, morning for us, afternoon i guess for you, yeah glad to be here.
[00:10] Marcus: hey all, marcus on platform, i'll mainly care about networking and infra questions.
[00:14] Rakesh: dr. rakesh mehta, research. i'll focus on model behavior and evals.
[00:18] Priya: great thanks, quick agenda: understand your workload, discuss model options (open models), context length and tool-calling, and then deployment options. we'll leave time at the end for next steps. sound good?
[00:27] Lena: perfect. just to set context, veridian is building an internal assistant for clinician summaries and adverse event triage. data is PHI, a mix of english and spanish notes, sometimes very long patient histories (think 40–80k tokens), and we need structured outputs to integrate into our adverse-event db. timeline is Q3 pilot, production later in year.
[00:45] Daniel: thanks, that's super helpful. when you mention 40–80k tokens, do you mean single-document notes or aggregations across visits?
[00:51] Lena: usually aggregation across visits, family notes, external records; some are scanned ocr'd text with noise too — so context plus robust extraction is key.
[00:58] Rakesh: and on quality, our bar for adverse-event extraction is pretty high — false positives are costly. we need deterministic structured outputs and strong grounding to source documents.
[01:08] Priya: understood. so two immediate technical constraints: long context, and tool-calling for retrieval + structured output. for models, are you open to hosted during pilot or do you require private/dedicated from day one?
[01:19] Lena: ideally private, but budget-wise we might do a hosted POC first if compliance docs and an agreement can be signed. if hosted is possible with a private VPC and strong encryption, we could start there.
[01:29] Marcus: just to add, our security team will insist on KMS integration and auditable request logs. can redwood provide that for hosted?
[01:35] Daniel: yes — hosted can be configured with customer-managed keys (KMS) and we have audit logs per request. we can also discuss retention policies and redaction during the POC. priya, do you want to go into models?
[01:44] Priya: sure. on open models, commonly we see customers testing Llama 3 variants, Mistral, Mixtral, and some RedPajama derivatives. for long context, there are a few paths: 1) models natively supporting longer windows (e.g., 32k+ or custom checkpoints at 64k/100k), 2) retrieval augmented generation where you chunk and retrieve, and 3) compressed KV cache strategies with our runtime. given 80k token windows, there are tradeoffs — running a native 100k-window model has higher memory and cost, whereas retrieval + tool-calling can keep costs manageable but adds complexity.
[02:22] Rakesh: are there reliable open models at 100k right now? we tested an experimental config but quality drops.
[02:28] Priya: there are a few bleeding-edge checkpoints that claim long windows — typically they are heavy and sometimes not as robust for hallucination. another approach is two-stage: use a dense retriever over preprocessed chunks, then call a smaller generator with the top-k chunks plus a dynamic context. that often gives better precision for extraction tasks.
[02:44] Lena: for clinical, hallucination is a showstopper. we need traceability back to source text. tool-calling to the adverse-event db and returning assertions with provenance is a requirement. can redwood support function/tool calling and structured outputs?
[02:56] Daniel: yes — our hosted API supports tool-calling and structured output schemas, and streaming. for Dedicated/Private we provide equivalent functionality and you can run connectors inside your VPC. priya, quick note on provenance?
[03:06] Priya: we can attach tokens to source chunk ids and return snippets with offsets, so the response can include a list of citations with start/end char indices. that ties into audit logs and helps you trace. there's some engineering work to standardize offsets for OCR'd docs but it's doable.
[03:23] Marcus: that sounds promising. what's the latency/cost profile if we do retrieval + small generator versus native long-context model?
[03:29] Priya: rough rule of thumb: native 100k model -> high GPU memory, so it's expensive per-token and higher latency for large requests. retrieval + 8k-32k generator -> lower token cost and faster end-to-end, but you trade off extra ops for retrieval and embedding index maintenance. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and caching strategies to shave costs.
[03:50] Rakesh: embeddings — are you recommending dense retrievers (faiss/pinecone) or we should use Redwood embeddings + internal vector store? our infra team prefers self-hosted faiss.
[03:59] Daniel: customers do both. Redwood will accept vectors we generate or you can bring your own. for Private/Dedicated you can host FAISS inside the same network and we can route retrieval calls there. hosted integrates with common vector stores as well.
[04:12] Lena: multilingual — our spanish notes are in regional clinical spanish with abbreviations. do models maintain parity across english/spanish, and what's your recommendation for multilingual?
[04:20] Priya: some open models are stronger in english; Mixtral and certain multilingual Mistral forks are better for Spanish. Often we fine-tune or use instruction-tuning on bilingual corpora. Another pragmatic approach: normalize via a small translation pass (high-quality clinical translator model) and then run extraction in English, but that can add latency and errors. If you need native multilingual performance we might prototype both approaches in the POC.
[04:44] Marcus: regulatory question — HIPAA compliance for hosted endpoints: what controls do we get?
[04:49] Daniel: hosted can be configured for HIPAA-safe processing via BAAs; we support customer-managed keys, VPC peering, private network paths, and retention policy controls. for customers with strict requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private so processing never leaves their environment.
[05:02] Lena: ok. cost question — what's a rough monthly for a small pilot (say 2k requests/day, avg 5k tokens)?
[05:09] Daniel: ballpark depends on model: with an efficient open model and retrieval, maybe low thousands/month on hosted. native long-context or Dedicated reserve changes the math — we can send a pricing matrix. i'll include low/med/high scenarios.
[05:20] Rakesh: how do we validate model quality? can priya propose an eval harness?
[05:24] Priya: yes. i'll propose a benchmark script: sample clinical notes sanitized, ground-truth annotations for extraction, and metrics (precision/recall/F1) plus latency and token cost. we'll run it across 3 model variants and retrieval vs native long-context. i'll provide expected artifacts and results format.
[05:39] Marcus: about deployment: if we go Dedicated, what's the SLA and autoscaling look like? we need predictable throughput for peak hours.
[05:46] Daniel: Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, configurable autoscaling and burst capacity. we have SLA tiers for latency and uptime; i'll include those SLAs in the packet. Dedicated also includes network isolation.
[05:56] Lena: and rollback/fallback behavior? if a model fails or is degraded, can you automatically fall back to a smaller model?
[06:02] Priya: yes, smart routing policies let you fallback to compatible model variants or route to a cheaper tier if latency is acceptable. you can set canary rollouts and automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to evals.
[06:13] Rakesh: for the structured output, we need schema validation and a guarantee that model outputs parse to JSON without hallucinated keys. do you enforce schema at runtime?
[06:22] Priya: we provide structured output tooling — you'll get a schema layer and a validator. For critical fields we recommend a strict post-validation step and if the model output fails schema, you can set automatic re-try with tightened prompts or escalate to human review.
[06:36] Marcus: what's the typical onboarding time for a Dedicated deployment?
[06:40] Daniel: depending on capacity and networking, 4–8 weeks for Dedicated (procurement dependent). Private on-prem can be longer — usually 8–12+ weeks. Hosted POC can start within days after paperwork.
[06:53] Lena: ok, sounds good. do you have specific references for pharma customers or compliance playbooks?
[06:58] Daniel: yes, i'll share redwood compliance summary and a sanitized case study for a health customer (redacted). also SOC2 report and our BAA template.
[07:06] Rakesh: one more technical: how does Redwood handle OCR'd noisy text? noisy tokens often break chunk boundaries.
[07:12] Priya: preprocessing is key — we'll recommend normalization steps, whitespace cleanup, and noise filtering. for chunking we can use semantic chunking anchored on clinical headings to preserve context. We can also configure fuzzy matching when retrieving.
[07:28] Lena: good. to recap, our immediate asks: security/compliance docs, pilot scope & pricing, sanitized sample dataset for benchmark, and a technical deep dive for infra.
[07:38] Daniel: correct. priya will draft the benchmark harness and i'll send pricing and compliance packet. we'll aim to follow up by next week.
[07:45] Marcus: can we include our infra lead on the technical deep dive? i'll loop them in.
[07:49] Daniel: please do.
[07:51] Lena: thanks everyone, this was useful. we'll review the docs and try to get the sample data sanitized and over to you.
[07:58] Daniel: perfect, talk soon. thanks all.

End of call.
